newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa govt yet to study Transnet pension report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa govt yet to study Transnet pension report.

text.p: The South African government has received but not yet studied a report on the 3.2 billion rand pension and medical aid fund deficit of the state-owned Transnet corporation, a minister said on Tuesday.

The 40-billion rand road, rail and air corporation ran up a massive pension fund deficit under apartheid, and efforts to refund the scheme have been hampered by huge payouts to senior officials taking retirement packages.
Minister of Public Enterprises Stella Sigcau told reporters she had received the report by government consultant Charles Stride but said it had not yet been submitted to the cabinet.
"That document is very important because when we deal with any restructuring of Transnet, these questions of the pension and medical aid funds will have to be addressed," she said.
A Public Enterprises Department official told Reuters the combined deficit of the Transnet pension and medical aid funds had been reduced since 1991 from 18 billion rand to around 3.2 billion rand.
He said, however, that the full or partial privatisation of separate Transnet entities could not be completed until the deficit had been apportioned or eliminated.
Sigcau said the pension deficit was holding up the search for a foreign minority shareholder for South African Airways (SAA), one of several state-owned companies earmarked for privatisation.
"We are seeing right now that the repositioning of SAA should be an immediate consideration, but you cannot talk repositioning of SAA without touching on what to do with the pension fund," she said.
"It's a complicated question and will have to be handled in such a manner that no group ends up being disadvantaged," she said.
The government has also given notice of its intention to fully privatise Autonet, a trucking subsidiary of Transnet and a participant in the same pension and medical aid funds.
Sigcau declined to say when the cabinet was likely to receive or act upon the Transnet report, which was commissioned last year.
"It's an initial report. We still have to discuss in cabinet and maybe, we will have questions. I've seen it, but I have not had time to read it thoroughly," she said.
